why: Post-order combine where the path must end at real leaves: each node returns its best path down to a leaf, and a node with two children joins its two best downward paths. Unlike max path sum, a negative branch cannot be dropped.
hints: Every leaf-to-leaf path has a highest node with two children. What does it take from each side?
down(leaf) = val; a node with one child must continue into it: down = val + down(child); a node with two children offers val + max(down(l), down(r)) upward and scores down(l) + down(r) + val.
One iterative post-order pass, keeping the best score over nodes with two children. O(n) time, 64-bit sums are fine in Python.
pitfalls: A node with one child is not a leaf; it cannot end the path and cannot skip its only child.
Do not clamp negative branches to 0 as in Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum; both endpoints must be leaves.
Only nodes with two children can be the bend of a leaf-to-leaf path.
